reads: Three corrections. (1) PAGES: the extract closes on n90 (stamp 94) at «pp. 276-278»; the row cited p.281–286. (2) DATE: the row read 1795-08-18. The Treaty of San Ildefonso — the Franco-Spanish alliance the row itself names — is of August 1796, and the surrounding leaves are 1796 material; the copy is undated and unplaced («Sin fecha ni lugar / Sin firma») and gives only «á 2 de Fructidor (23 de Agosto) y ratificada en 26 del mismo por el consejo de los Ancianos en Paris», so the year is supplied from the treaty's identity, not transcribed from the leaf. (3) CONTENT: the row glossed art. 18 as «mutual navigation rights». It is not — art. 18 provides that England being the only power against whom Spain has direct grievances, the alliance shall operate against her alone during the present war, Spain remaining neutral toward the other powers armed against France. The summary now carries the articles as transcribed (4, 5, 18). ⚠ FOURTH correction, found by an adversarial re-read 2026-09-09: the row's own VERBATIM quotation was mistranscribed. Savage writes «Yldefonso» with a capital Y, joins his words as «yla Republica» and «delos Ancianos», and accents «à 2 de Fructidor». The copy is also a SELECTIVE extract beginning at article 4 (arts. 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 15, 18 only), not the whole treaty. And the row previously glossed art. 5 as «18,000 infantry and 6,000 horse»: the manuscript reads «189 infantes y 69 Caballos». Those are the treaty's real figures abbreviated or miscopied, but the record now carries what Savage wrote, with the discrepancy noted.

reads: Leaf n383 (stamp 385 / ink 190), entry 2 of the Los Ángeles February 1797 diary, read at scale 1 on a full-resolution crop: «la de Cornelio Abela con **40** fanegas de mais propio, la de Quinto Suniga con 24 fanegas de mais propio, la de Bartolo Topia con 27 fanegas de mais propio, todos los dichos para el presidio de S.n Diego». **The Avila figure is 40, not 450**; the glyph is a 4 followed by a 0, the same width as the adjacent 24 and 27, and 40 is of a piece with them. note: Figure correction from a full-resolution crop, 2026-09-22. The row is otherwise sound and was not rewritten.

was: Fragments of the burst cannon reached the church, “145 varas” away.
reads: Full-resolution re-read of the leaf: “… algunos de los cuales llegaron hasta la Yglesia, 125 varas; lo disparó Sold.o Alejandro Arriola.” The figure is 125, not 145.
note: Savage enters the item under a 21 Jul 1792 Sal→Arrillaga heading as a sub-entry dated “Sete. 30.” Only the feast name (“q.e se hace á las Llagas de S.n Fran.co”) stands in Savage's quotation marks; the burst, the ten pieces and the distance are his reported speech, not the document's words.

was: A vault transcription of this leaf gave the quoted close as “Según sus informes, quieren los ingleses…” and stated the reading had been verified at full resolution.
reads: Full-resolution re-read: “Segun sus espresiones, quieren los ingleses la boca de este puerto por línea divisoria: salió cierto que dos fragatas de aquella Nacion estuvieron en la Bodega.” The word is espresiones. The catalog record was already right; the transcription file was wrong and has been corrected.
note: Savage's quotation marks open at “Segun” and close after “Bodega”: that sentence alone carries the document's own wording. The preceding burst-cannon clause — “que el presidio solo tenía un cañon, y ese reventado hace muchos años” — is Savage's third-person report and must not be printed as Sal's words. Note also “hace muchos años”: on 31 Oct 1792 the presidio's single gun is described as having burst long before, which does not describe the fiesta burst of 30 Sept 1792 recorded at ca55-d136.

was: The ships had been “ashore 4 days & still there”, and asked the Indians for cattle “showing them otters beforehand”.
reads: Full-resolution re-read of n66–n67. Savage quotes Sal throughout: “había dos barcos en el P.to de la Bodega; preguntado p.r mí me respondió, no entendían lo q.e les hablaban, y q.e los soldados traían ropa como nuestras vueltas, de q.e colegí serían ingleses; vuelto á preguntar, dijo q.e habían estado había 4 lunas, y no permanecían á la presente, q.e habían cogido agua, leña, y cazado muchos venados, y q.e á los indios les pedían ganado enseñándoles astas de res.”
note: Four corrections. (1) FOUR MOONS, not four days. (2) They were NO LONGER THERE — “no permanecían á la presente”. (3) They showed the Indians CATTLE HORNS (astas de res), not otters. (4) “English” is Sal's own inference from the clothing (“de q.e colegí serían ingleses”), not the informant's statement. The four-moon duration independently corroborates ca54-d161, where Sal reports from the same indigenous channel that the English had frequented Bodega “más de seis meses”.

was: “Sal reports that the establishment of the puerto de Bodega will not be carried out”, with “no se efectuará el establecimiento del puerto de Bodega” treated elsewhere as a quotation from Sal.
reads: Full-resolution re-read of n354. The entry in full: “Le dice que entendiendo que no se efectuará el establecim.to del puerto de Bodega, ha aplicado á los usos del presidio de S.n Fr.co varios artículos que se habían destinado p.a Bodega.”
note: There are no quotation marks anywhere in this entry, so the phrase is Savage's reported speech and not Sal's words. And the governing participle is ENTENDIENDO: Sal acts on his own understanding that the establishment will not happen. The entry records no order of abandonment — it records a commandant reallocating stores because he has concluded nothing further is coming.
